The clause is $(\neg A \lor B)$. If $A$ is false (Dr. Johnson is NOT doing it), then $B$ must be true. Or simply, at least one of the two options holds.
    *   Let's look at the structure carefully. "Either P or Q" translates to $(P \lor Q)$.
    *   Crucially, many conditions involve negations of the *same* variable pair (e.g., $\neg x(A,B,C) \lor x(D,E,F)$). These form XNOR relationships or direct equivalences between specific assignments.
